transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Hernandez, Sofia, thank you for coming back in. I wanted to sit down with you both to talk about why you had to return to the emergency department last night.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am just tired. My leg hurts very much.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: She says she’s exhausted and the pain in her leg is very bad.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that you are in a lot of pain and that this is incredibly draining for you. I want to take as much time as we need to talk through this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why did this happen? We were told she was ready to go yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There were some issues with the timing of the discharge and things didn't go quite right with the protocol.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What does that mean? The wound is open. Why was she sent home if it wasn't right?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry for any confusion and the stress this caused. We were very busy on the floor yesterday, and some of the steps were rushed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Busy? My mother is seventy years old. She is bleeding through the bandage. Was it a mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is very difficult to be in this position, and I can tell how frustrating and scary this is for you both.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is scary. I feel like I cannot trust the doctors here now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear that you're feeling a loss of trust. It's completely understandable that you would feel that way after having to come back in the middle of the night.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what happened? Exactly?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, there was a mix-up with the discharge process. We had some confusion regarding the timing.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not an answer. Did someone forget to check the wound? Did the doctor not look at her?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The process just didn't happen according to the usual timing.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. Were you supposed to keep her longer?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had some challenges with the workflow yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Sofia, ask him if they made a mistake.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Did you make a mistake? Tell us clearly.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry this has been so confusing. As I mentioned, the timing was off.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: She is still hurting. She is shaking.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I see her shaking. I can tell this is overwhelming for you, Mrs. Hernandez. We are going to stay right here until we get this sorted.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want her to be okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are going to make sure she is okay. I have a very specific plan for us now. First, I have already consulted with the surgical lead, and we have scheduled a wound revision for tomorrow morning at 8:00 AM to properly close the site.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Tomorrow? She stays here tonight?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, she will stay in a monitored bed tonight. I have ordered a continuous IV antibiotic drip starting right now to prevent any further infection. I will personally check her wound every four hours tonight to monitor the drainage.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And then what?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Once the revision is done tomorrow, you will both meet with the wound care nurse at 2:00 PM to learn exactly how to change the dressings at home, and Sofia, I'll give you a checklist so you can help her track the temperature and color of the skin.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will this happen again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: To make sure this doesn't happen to anyone else, I am filing a formal incident report today. I'm also meeting with the nursing supervisor tomorrow morning to change how our discharge checklists are signed off so that no one leaves before the protocol time is met.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know why she was sent home early.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it's frustrating that I can't give you a different answer, but there were issues with the system's timing yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I still don't understand the "timing."

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The main thing is that we are focused on the recovery now. I will be the one overseeing her care until the surgery tomorrow. Do you have any other questions about the surgery or the antibiotics?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No. Just please fix her leg.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are going to do everything we can to get her healed. I'll be back in twenty minutes to check the IV.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient to finish all turns, remains regulated under repeated pushback, and uses no rushing language.

E.justification: The resident never explicitly names the error, relying entirely on platitudes and vague hedging such as 'things didn't go quite right' and 'issues with the timing'.

A.justification: While the resident says 'I am sorry', responsibility is consistently deflected to 'the protocol', 'the floor', and 'the system's timing'.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions ('frustrating', 'scary', 'overwhelming', 'loss of trust') and references the patient's specific distress.

T.justification: The resident provides specific steps with timelines (8:00 AM surgery, 2:00 PM nurse meeting), a named patient role (checklist for Sofia), and a prevention plan (incident report and checklist change).
